renders.title: Why Bitcoin Got Everything and Still Fell
renders.bestFor: an audience that already holds the wrong model
renders.weakness: can read as contrarian if the steel-man is cut

beats.label: SCQA · situation
beats.text: Last October, Bitcoin set the highest price in its history.

beats.label: the wish list, delivered
beats.text: Then it received almost everything it had asked for: a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve, friendly regulators, retirement accounts.

beats.label: the complication
beats.text: And in the same months it lost roughly half its value.

beats.label: the question aloud
beats.text: What went wrong?

beats.label: the answer, stated early
beats.text: Nothing went wrong. Getting what it asked for is the reason the price stopped rising.

beats.label: three topics, one breath
beats.text: To see why: where the fund money went, what happened to the buyers who would never sell, and why approval did not matter.

beats.label: M1 · where the money went
beats.text: The fund inflows were real. More demand against a fixed supply should lift a price. That is the model almost everyone used.

beats.label: M1 · and the hedging
beats.text: Authorised participants often create and short fund shares before they buy any bitcoin. The inflow is a booking, not a purchase.

beats.label: M2 · the buyers who would never sell
beats.text: A treasury company could issue shares and buy more bitcoin while the market valued it above its holdings.

beats.label: TURN 2 · the machine only turns one way
beats.text: When that premium fell below one, the buying stopped, and Strategy sold for the first time.

beats.label: the script attacks its own argument
beats.text: These are not forced sellers. Strategy holds a cash reserve for years of payments, and long-term holders bought again after the crash.

beats.label: M3 · why Washington did not matter
beats.text: The reserve order should have ended the argument about legitimacy.

beats.label: TURN 3 · the reserve that was never built
beats.text: It still is not built, and agencies cannot agree how much bitcoin the government owns.

beats.label: reframe, not summary
beats.text: Adoption succeeded, and the prize for winning was being absorbed into the system it set out to escape. The price is not broken. The story is.

cutFacts.why: the share-price fall restates the premium collapse the mNAV beat already carries

renders.title: Three Answers to a Falling Bitcoin
renders.bestFor: an audience that has heard every explanation and believes none
renders.weakness: the candidates can blur if the verdict comes late

beats.label: the puzzle
beats.text: Bitcoin got the policy wins it wanted and still lost roughly half its value.

beats.label: the question aloud
beats.text: Why did the price not rise?

beats.label: three candidates
beats.text: Three answers compete: the fund plumbing, the treasury companies, and the macro weather.

beats.label: candidate one · plumbing
beats.text: Fund inflows are not immediate spot demand, and sellers absorbed the buying that did arrive.

beats.label: candidate two · the flywheel stalls
beats.text: The treasury flywheel only works while the market pays a premium, and that premium is gone.

beats.label: candidate three · macro
beats.text: Analysts point to the dollar, tariffs and central bank policy outweighing regulatory progress.

beats.label: against the verdict
beats.text: Long-term holders kept accumulating after the drawdown, which is not what a capitulation looks like.

beats.label: the verdict
beats.text: The candidates are one story: bitcoin now trades as a risk asset inside portfolios, moving with stocks rather than against them.

beats.label: reframe
beats.text: It won the argument for legitimacy, and legitimacy made it ordinary.
